steps.label: Ask if unsure
steps.ask: How can I tell what someone is feeling?

faq.a: Body language is how your face, hands, arms and the way you stand show your feelings without words. People read it all the time, often without noticing.

faq.q: What do eyes say in body language?
faq.a: Looking at someone often shows you are listening or interested. Looking away can mean shy, bored or upset. But customs differ, and some people look away to show respect.
Crossed arms can mean someone feels cross, worried or closed off. But they might just be cold or comfy, so check other clues too.

faq.q: How can I tell what someone is feeling?
faq.a: Put the clues together: face, body, voice and words. If you are still unsure, ask kindly: You look a bit quiet, are you okay?
asks: Tell me about the Ask if unsure

faq.q: Is body language the same everywhere?
faq.a: Some things, like smiling, are understood almost everywhere. Others change: a nod means yes in most countries, but can mean no in Bulgaria, and a head wobble means okay in parts of South India.
asks: Does body language change in different countries?

facts: Research by Paul Ekman found that facial expressions for basic feelings like happiness and fear are recognised across many cultures.
In Bulgaria, nodding the head can mean no and shaking it can mean yes.
